$comment: Memory item v2 contract (context pipeline §13). Clients run their production canonicalizer, legacy migration, injection filter and sync merge on each input. Server-time fields are null in expectations (the store sets them on write) and must be ignored when comparing written documents.

constants.organizeSystemPrompt: Split the saved memory below into separate items. Each item states exactly one fact, preference, instruction, constraint or project. Keep the user's language and wording; do not add, infer, merge away or drop information. Reply with only a JSON array, no prose: [{"kind": "identity|preference|instruction|constraint|project|goal|decision|fact", "content": "..."}].

rules: Canonical: fill defaults, lowercase id / mutationId / conflictGroupId / supersedes, keep content byte-for-byte.
Migration id = UUIDv5(namespace, uid + \n + legacyKey); mutationId = UUIDv5(namespace, id + \n + migration-1); write with create-if-absent.

memoryText non-blank → one fact item, status active, content = memoryText unchanged. antiForgetText non-blank and trim(antiForgetText) != trim(memoryText) → one instruction item, status active when Anti-Forget was enabled, paused when disabled.
status paused = kept and editable, never injected (also the per-item off switch in settings).

Injectable: layer semantic, status active, expiresAt null or > now, scope global / this conversation / this folder (scope.id compared case-insensitively: UUID ids differ in case across clients). instruction + constraint → standingInstructions, others → memory; pinned first then input order. restricted items are injected into the user's own chat provider but never cloud-synced, never sent to memoryExtraction, never in telemetry.

Merge: a pending local edit whose baseRevision is behind a remote revision with different content → conflicted (both kept); a remote echo of the pending mutationId confirms it; otherwise a higher remote revision applies (tombstones included), equal revision + same mutationId is a no-op, lower is ignored.

Order: list order = pinned first, then createdAt ascending (null first, compared as instants), then id ascending. Injection input, settings list, raw view, legacy compile and backup export all use it.

Tombstone: delete keeps id, schemaVersion, layer, kind, createdAt; status deleted, content "", deletedAt = deletion time, revision unchanged until pushed, baseRevision = revision, new mutationId / deviceId; every other field back to defaults (no body, no source pointers).

Merge additions: a remote at or below the pending baseRevision → keepPending; no pending and same revision with another mutationId → applyRemote (server wins); a pending delete always wins (keepPending, pushed at remote revision + 1); a pending edit meeting a newer remote tombstone is dropped (deletion is never resurrected by an offline edit); a pending edit equal in content and status to the newer remote is dropped as applyRemote.

Push (inside a remote-store transaction): remote missing → write revision 1; remote mutationId = pending mutationId → confirmed, no write; pending baseRevision 0 (a create: migration, conflict copy, new item) with a remote present → dropPending (create-if-absent; the listener merge applies the remote the same way); remote revision = pending baseRevision → write remote revision + 1; otherwise apply the merge additions (pending delete → write remote revision + 1; remote tombstone or same content → dropPending) and anything else is a conflict.

Conflict: the original item takes the remote content and becomes status conflicted with conflictGroupId = its own id (a normal local edit, pushed); the pending edit becomes a copy with id = UUIDv5(namespace, itemId + \n + pendingMutationId), status conflicted, conflictGroupId = itemId, revision 1, baseRevision 0, mutationId = UUIDv5(namespace, copyId + \n + conflict-1), createdAt / updatedAt null. Resolving keeps one (status active, conflictGroupId null) and tombstones the other.

Legacy compile (dual write for one release cycle): memoryText = contents of semantic, active, non-restricted, global items except the Anti-Forget migration id, in list order, joined by \n\n; memoryTextDigest = sha256 hex of its UTF-8. When memoryText changes, new clients write memoryText, memoryTextDigest and memoryUpdatedAt = now together and push them; a write that only fills a missing / stale digest (textChanged false) stays local: memoryUpdatedAt untouched, nothing pushed (a fresh device must never overwrite the cloud memoryText before its first pull). Anti-Forget fields are never written again.

Legacy sync (migrated is a per-account local flag): not migrated and memoryTextDigest = sha256(memoryText) → the account was migrated by another new client: create nothing, just set the flag. Not migrated otherwise → migration items created if absent. Migrated and digest = sha256(memoryText) → nothing. Otherwise an old client edited memoryText: if it equals the compile only the prefs are rewritten; blank → tombstone the memoryText migration item; else that item gets content = memoryText, status active (created when missing). Its mutationId = UUIDv5(namespace, itemId + \n + legacy- + sha256(text, or "" when text is White_Space-only)) so every device makes the same mutation. writePrefs = { memoryText, memoryTextDigest, textChanged } when memoryText or digest differ from the compile, else null; textChanged = compile differs from memoryText.

Raw view: render = contents of semantic active items in list order joined by \n---\n. Apply: identical text → no ops. Split on lines equal to --- (a trailing \r ignored), trim each segment (White_Space), drop empty ones; a segment over contentMaxCodePoints → error tooLong with its index (0-based, counted after empty segments are dropped). Pass 1: each segment keeps the first unmatched item whose trimmed content equals it. Pass 2: remaining segments update remaining items pairwise in order; extra segments create kind fact items (ids supplied by the caller); extra items are deleted.

Organize: request = system organizeSystemPrompt, one user message = the item content unchanged. Parse = text from the first [ to the last ], JSON array; keep objects with a string content, trimmed (White_Space), non-empty, ≤ contentMaxCodePoints, not a duplicate; kind lowercased when it is one of the eight semantic kinds else fact; at most organizeMaxItems. Anything unparseable → []. Accepting creates source manual items; the original is tombstoned unless the user keeps it.

Backup: top-level memorySchemaVersion 2 and memoryItems = every local item (tombstones and conflicts included) in list order, canonical, server-time fields as RFC3339 or null. Import merge per id: missing locally or backup revision higher → take the backup item; otherwise keep local (a tombstone is not resurrected by an older backup). Replace takes the backup list, and every live local item missing from the backup becomes a pending tombstone (tombstonedIds) so the cloud and other devices converge; importNew only adds ids missing locally (tombstones count as present). Imported items are pending and go through Push. A backup without memoryItems is migrated from its legacy preferences (create if absent).

Remote document = all fieldOrder keys of the canonical item; revision / baseRevision from Push (remote missing → revision 1, baseRevision 0 regardless of local values); unknown kind / status read from storage fall back to fact / paused (kept, never injected); updatedAt = server timestamp; createdAt = server timestamp on create, the remote value on update. restricted items are never written (skip).

Restricted retraction (P6): a pending item with sensitivity restricted is never written as itself. Push reads the remote in the same transaction: remote live (status not deleted, any revision) → retract = write the item's tombstone (Tombstone rule; mutationId and deviceId = the pending item's, deletedAt = now, sensitivity back to normal) at remote revision + 1 with baseRevision = remote revision; remote missing or already a tombstone → localOnly, no write. Either way the local item keeps its content, status and restricted sensitivity, becomes synced, and its revision = baseRevision = the written revision (retract), the remote tombstone revision, or 0 (missing). Merge: a local item that is restricted ignores every remote version (ignoreRemote; keepPending when it has a pending change), so the retraction echo and later edits from devices that still had the copy never overwrite it. Other devices apply the tombstone like any delete. Absent sensitivity in a case input means normal.

migrationCases.note: id and mutationId are deterministic, so two devices migrating create one item (create-if-absent).
The user had switched Anti-Forget off: keep the text (no loss) but do not inject it (status paused).
Migration never truncates; the 2000 code point limit applies to edits.

injectableCases.note: iOS stores conversation ids as uppercase UUID strings, Web / Android lowercase.

mergeCases.note: A late edit from an offline device never resurrects a deleted item.
Pending local edit based on revision 2 meets a different revision 3: keep both as conflicted, never overwrite silently.
Deleted on another device while this one edited offline: the deletion stands.
baseRevision 0 is a create-if-absent (migration on a second device): an existing remote wins, never a conflict.
Cannot happen with transactional writes; if it does, the server copy wins.
